title: Close the parity suite's false-green paths
action: S3 judge findings F1, F3, F4, F5 — the suite can report green while proving nothing. (F1, blocker) opencode_plugin_contracts.rs:314-321's node_or_skip prints to captured stderr and returns, so a shell whose node predates v24 (e.g. /usr/bin/node v18 without nvm on PATH) yields 4 green tests and zero enforcement coverage; make the skip impossible to mistake for coverage — the suite must FAIL when the capability is absent unless an explicit opt-out env var is set, and the skip reason must reach the default (captured) output either way. Decide and record which, matching how this project treats environment-gated proof elsewhere. (F3) every stub swallows stdin (cat >/dev/null) and fixtures pass generic args, so a field-name mistranslation fails OPEN and stays green — assert the payload bee actually receives for each mapped row: real field names (filePath/command/patchText and the read-shaped ones), tool_name, cwd, session id. (F4) the plugin-side floor is a hand-written pairs.len() >= 9 and the belt check only asks whether >=1 tool routes to a hook — derive the tool inventory from the installed OpenCode binary's own registry (the same evidence oc-3 used) and fail when a registered write- or read-capable tool has no mapping, so the apply_patch defect class cannot recur; two registered tools already fall through today (list, lsp — lsp returns file content for an arbitrary filePath) and discovery.md:332-345's 13-tool enumeration is incomplete. (F5) the named-gap assertion ANDs a per-rule contains() with a document-global literal that is always present (discovery.md:560-561), so any mention anywhere passes — scope the check to the rule's own row. Update discovery.md's runner-design section to match.

truths: A node-incapable environment cannot produce a green enforcement suite by default
Each mapped row asserts the exact payload bee receives — a renamed field fails the test
The tool inventory is derived from the installed binary; an unmapped registered write/read tool fails by name
The named-gap check is scoped to its own rule's row, not the whole document

trace.outcome: Closed F1/F3/F4/F5 in the OpenCode parity suite: fail-by-default (opt-out env var) on missing node/opencode capability, exact per-row payload+D6 verdict assertions, binary-derived tool-registry coverage gate (caught real unmapped lsp tool by name), and a properly line-scoped named-gap check; plugin left unchanged, lsp/list recorded as named gaps in discovery.md
